implementation_state: The offline release gate exists and can refuse. It replays a recorded decision from the retained decision-time input through the same accepted path the original took, requires the result to be bit-identical to the record, judges it against the canonical Outcome, keys on the identity that actually served, consumes 7E-2D's calibration verdict without reinterpreting it, and derives one recomputed verdict whose every constituent is visible. It is evidence, not activation.
unblock_condition: Satisfied. All four required gates hold, with the statistical portion explicitly deferred to 7D under the E-092 boundary rather than half-built: this node owns the gate wiring and the verdict, 7D owns attempt-level attribution and the statistical release methodology.
notes: REPLAY EQUIVALENCE IS BIT-IDENTICAL AND MAY NOT BE APPROXIMATE. Every float is compared through to_bits, never through ==, so +0.0 and -0.0 are correctly a divergence. There is no epsilon, no rounding and no partial comparison anywhere in the module; a sweep of the new file for tolerance constructs found none. Any non-identical result is a typed refusal naming the FIRST differing component in a fixed documented order, not a pass with a small delta.

The non-finite check runs BEFORE any comparison, and only on the recorded side. That asymmetry is deliberate and sufficient: under to_bits two same-bit NaNs would score a match, and guarding the recorded side means a replayed NaN necessarily diverges from a guaranteed-finite value instead of matching it.

The replay is driven through the same accepted ShadowEngine::evaluate_with path the original decision took, on purpose. A second independent implementation could only have shown that the two implementations differ, which is a fact about the gate; sharing the path means a divergence can only mean the retained input or the commit is not the one the original used, which is a fact about the evidence.

No journal-carried f64 is a compared component, and that exclusion is documented in the module header rather than left as an accident of which fields happen to be compared. This is what keeps the gate decidable while E-089's float hazard is live on the read path.

The f32 feature vectors are asserted to survive the same read path, and that is a MEASUREMENT, not a proof. A double-rounding counterexample is possible though very unlikely, and its consequence is a REFUSAL, not a false pass, so it limits how often the gate can reach a verdict rather than whether a wrong verdict is safe.

THE RELEASE VERDICT IS RECOMPUTED. ReleaseVerdict::from_measurements reads the measurements and nothing else; there is no stored boolean anywhere on the report that it could disagree with, and no path reaching Considerable without every constituent measured. The blockers are exposed so a reader sees WHICH measurement refused. NotConsiderable is the honest default, because we-cannot-show-it and we-have-shown-it are different claims.

EvidenceFloors is a PRESENCE floor, not a significance test, and says so in the type, the module header and the commit message. No confidence interval, power analysis, significance test, minimum detectable effect, multiple-comparison control or bootstrap exists anywhere in this node; a sweep for those constructs found only prose declaring their absence. All of it is 7D's under E-092.

The gate cannot name ml::activation, and an earlier design that imported CommitFile, SnapshotFile and snapshot_id_for was REJECTED BY THE 7E-2F BOUNDARY TEST rather than worked around. The installer staying unreachable from the ML stack is the correct constraint, so the import was removed rather than the check weakened.

Consequence of that boundary, recorded because it is a real limit and not a detail: the only bit-exact model persistence in the repository lives in the module this gate may not name. See E-097, which is OPEN and blocks nothing here but must be resolved before 7F.

A design error was caught mid-implementation by the worker and is worth recording because the corrected version is load-bearing: the holdout was first built from request-scope samples alone, reasoning that attempt-level rows belong to 7D. Reading project_cohorts showed it skips SampleScope::Request rows when building the candidate axis, so that design would have handed the calibration measurement a one-candidate axis and a trivially perfect vector, making calibrated vacuous. Every canonical row is now carried, and a test asserts the holdout is DECISIONS * (axis + 1) rows.

The worker also reported a PRE-EXISTING flake in a file outside its diff, performance_10k_extractions, which is recorded as E-095 rather than dismissed. Together with E-094 that is two wall-clock budgets in this project that fail only under concurrent load. Neither is attributed to any code change and neither is closed.
